subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Chemical reactions as the rearrangement of atoms
Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
Representing reactions with word and symbol equations
Acids, alkalis and the pH scale

questions.lo: Chemical reactions as the rearrangement of atoms
questions.q: What happens to atoms during a chemical reaction?
options: They are destroyed and new atoms are created
They are rearranged into new substances
They stay bonded in exactly the same way
questions.explain: In a reaction the bonds between atoms are broken and remade, so the same atoms end up joined in new ways. Atoms are never created or destroyed.

questions.lo: Chemical reactions as the rearrangement of atoms
questions.q: Which of these is a chemical reaction rather than just a physical change?
options: Wood burning to make ash and gases
questions.explain: A chemical reaction makes new substances. Burning wood makes new substances (ash, gases), so it is a reaction. Melting, dissolving and boiling are physical changes with no new substance.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: In a sealed container, 30 g of reactants react completely. What is the total mass of the products?
questions.explain: Mass is conserved because atoms are only rearranged. The products must have the same total mass as the reactants: 30 g.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: A candle burns and seems to lose mass. Why is mass still conserved?
options: Some atoms were destroyed by the flame
Gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour escaped into the air
New atoms were created in the wax
questions.explain: The candle looks lighter only because gases float away. If you captured all the gases, the total mass would be unchanged — mass is always conserved.

questions.lo: Representing reactions with word and symbol equations
questions.q: In a word equation, where do the products go?
options: On the left of the arrow
On the right of the arrow
questions.explain: Reactants go on the left and products (the new substances made) go on the right. The arrow means 'reacts to make'.

questions.lo: Representing reactions with word and symbol equations
questions.q: How many hydrogen atoms are shown on the left of the balanced equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O?
questions.explain: 2H₂ means 2 molecules of H₂, and each has 2 hydrogen atoms: 2 × 2 = 4 hydrogen atoms. The right side also has 4 (2 × H₂O), so it is balanced.

questions.q: What is always needed for combustion (burning) to happen?
questions.explain: Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that releases energy as heat and light. Without oxygen a fuel cannot burn.

questions.q: When a fuel undergoes complete combustion in plenty of air, which products form?
questions.explain: Complete combustion of a carbon-and-hydrogen fuel gives carbon dioxide and water. Carbon monoxide and soot form only in incomplete combustion (too little oxygen).

questions.q: Heating calcium carbonate gives calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. What type of reaction is this?
questions.explain: Heat breaks one compound down into two or more simpler substances — that is thermal decomposition ('thermal' = heat, 'decomposition' = breaking apart).

questions.q: In an oxidation reaction, a substance...
questions.explain: Oxidation means gaining oxygen. Rusting (iron + oxygen → iron oxide) and burning are both examples of oxidation.

questions.q: An iron nail is placed in blue copper sulfate solution. It becomes coated with copper and the blue fades. Why?
options: Iron is less reactive, so copper displaces it
Iron is more reactive, so it displaces copper from the compound
The iron is being oxidised by the air
questions.explain: In a displacement reaction the more reactive metal takes the place of the less reactive one. Iron is more reactive than copper, so it pushes copper out of copper sulfate.

questions.lo: Acids, alkalis and the pH scale
questions.q: What pH value is neutral?
questions.explain: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14. pH 7 is neutral (like pure water). pH 0 is a very strong acid and pH 14 a very strong alkali.

questions.lo: Acids, alkalis and the pH scale
questions.q: A liquid has a pH of 2. What does this tell you?
questions.explain: Low pH numbers mean acidic. A pH of 2 is well below 7, so the liquid is a strong acid.

questions.q: A few drops of universal indicator turn a solution green. What is the solution?
questions.explain: Universal indicator is green at pH 7, which is neutral. Red/orange shows acid and blue/purple shows alkali.

questions.q: What colour does litmus turn in an alkali?
questions.explain: Litmus turns red in acid and blue in alkali. A handy way to remember: 'blue for basic/alkali'.

questions.q: What are the products when an acid reacts with an alkali (neutralisation)?
questions.explain: Neutralisation always makes a salt and water: acid + alkali → salt + water. The pH moves towards 7.

questions.q: Someone has an acidic stomach and takes an indigestion tablet. What kind of substance must the tablet contain to help?
questions.explain: An alkali (base) neutralises the excess stomach acid, moving the pH back towards neutral and easing the discomfort.

questions.q: Magnesium is added to hydrochloric acid and bubbles fizz off. Which gas is produced?
questions.explain: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen. The fizzing bubbles are hydrogen gas, which gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint.

questions.q: Which pair of products forms when a metal reacts with an acid?
questions.explain: Metal + acid → salt + hydrogen. Do not confuse this with neutralisation (acid + alkali → salt + water).

questions.q: Which statement about a catalyst is correct?
options: It slows a reaction down and is used up
It speeds a reaction up and is not used up
It changes which products are made
It is one of the reaction's products
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up a reaction without being used up, so it can be recovered and used again. It does not change the products.
